name: Sanni Oluwanifemi
missingPieces: D3 report surfaced only 4 of 10 findings; decoy in D3 stated incorrectly; no exact log field or false-positive rate on detection stopgaps; single chain-level CVSS instead of per-finding vectors; D4 does not clearly own all four prompts.
feedback: D1 is the strongest deliverable. You catalogued all ten findings with an OWASP category, a CWE, and a pack specific evidence line for each, and that is exactly the level of proof the key rewards. SQL injection A03 CWE-89 at 02:15:31, unsalted MD5 A02 CWE-916 at line 62/69, JWT alg:none A07 CWE-347 on Token 2, no expiry A07 CWE-613, stored XSS at 02:18:47, XXE with the file:///etc/passwd entity, path traversal at 02:24:02 and open redirect at 02:21:13 are all correctly placed. Two smaller points cost you here. You labelled the hardcoded secret as CWE-321 weak secret rather than CWE-798 hardcoded credential, which I accepted as a defensible class variant, but you swapped the cookie missing Secure/SameSite finding (A05 CWE-614) for an error disclosure entry, so the tenth canonical finding is absent. Your decoy verdict named the b64url helpers and called them clean, which is an accepted safe construct, but your proof stayed at the encoding layer and never engaged the real mechanism, that the HS256 verify branch is sound because hash_equals is constant time while the actual bugs are alg:none and the hardcoded secret. D2 chains SQLi to JWT to XXE to exfil with verbatim PoC for each hop, and the forged none token and the XXE XML are reproduced cleanly, which I credited. What is missing is the full ordered chain, you collapsed eight hops into four and dropped the stored XSS and open redirect steps that belong in sequence, and your CVSS is a single chain level CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H scored 10.0 rather than a justified vector per finding. The SQLi bypass does not touch availability, so its vector should read A:N giving roughly 9.1, not A:H. Your impact of 312 customers and about 67 million naira traces to the exfil sample and sits inside the expected tens of millions band, so that is real and not penalised, though you should state the per customer balance as an assumption. D3 reads well and ends on the naira headline, the threat model with The Griot and the Tor exit node is present, and your remediation is ordered by effort in hours which is what the key asks for. Two things hurt this section. Your decoy clarification is wrong, you described phishing and PHPSESSID as the red herring and the forged JWT as the truth, which is the investigation narrative, not the safe construct disproof the brief wanted about the b64url and hash_equals code. Your two detection stopgaps name no exact log field and no false positive rate, and you even note that yourself, so that row could not score above a third. D4 cites ISC2 Canon 1, 2 and 4 by number and load bearing, and it ties NDPA Section 40 and the 72 hour NDPC notification to the breach, but it runs as one continuous stance rather than clearly owning all four prompts, the colleague evidence question and the one action regardless of the manager are not distinctly answered, and you omitted Section 41 on notifying the 312 data subjects on high risk. I looked hard for a way to push this into the 70s given how complete D1 is, and the honest reason it lands at 63 is that D2 and D3 carry the partial chain, the single wrong CVSS vector, the incorrect decoy and the missing detection specifics. The single most important fix is to defend a complete per finding CVSS vector with one justifying sentence each, starting by correcting the SQLi to AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N.
